_comment: ccc-agent runtime config. Install (root-owned, world-readable) at /etc/ccc-agent/config.json or /opt/ccc-agent/config/config.json. The agent must never be able to write this file or anything under state_dir. In CCC images this file is generated at container startup by ccc-agent setup (it needs runtime-only paths: the container name + /storage layout), NOT at image build.
_state_comment: Holds the BranchFS mountpoints, so it MUST be under a CCC bind mount (the FUSE sidecar refuses the container overlay like /opt). /storage/user always is; it is hidden from the branch via hide_paths. For node-local speed use a bind-mounted local scratch, e.g. /storage/local/ssd/.ccc-agent.
_alias_comment: home_subdir feeds the policy alias /home/<user> -> /storage/user/<home_subdir>. CCC mounts the user home to the same bytes as /storage/user/<container>, so set this to the container name to dedup them in policy.
_workspace_comment: Launch workspace is per invocation: ccc-agent run defaults to the caller's current directory; pass --workspace to override.
_confinement_comment: bwrap = real rootless sandbox (default). none = debug only, NOT a boundary.
_run_access_comment: Default true: bind the existing CCC/container /run runtime namespace, read-only /var, and device-capable /dev into bwrap so agents can use container-provided sockets/devices (Docker via /var/run/docker.sock or /run/docker.sock, ssh-agent, /dev/fuse, etc.). Rootless bwrap maps the uid plus one gid, not every supplementary group; when Docker socket access depends on a supplementary group, ccc-agent maps that socket gid automatically. Set bwrap_gid explicitly to override. Set container_run_access false, or run ccc-agent run --full-isolation, for no-ambient-runtime mode. This protects normal /home and /storage writes, not full escape prevention from a container that already exposes powerful sockets/devices.
_runtime_comment: The agent binary + deps live under the real $HOME / storage that the view hides; re-expose them read-only here. Prefer dests OUTSIDE the views (e.g. install agents at /opt) to avoid bwrap mkdir'ing mountpoints into the FUSE view. 'src' or 'src:dest'.
_agent_state_comment: Default: ~/.codex, ~/.claude, and ~/.hermes are shared rw agent/system state, direct-bound over the BranchFS home view and therefore outside ccc-agent commit/review/rollback. Codex/Claude/Hermes own concurrent access to their state. Set protect_agent_state=true or pass ccc-agent run --protect-agent-state to keep these dirs inside BranchFS instead.
_cred_comment: Do NOT bind the whole ~/.codex, ~/.claude, or ~/.hermes read-only: Codex/Claude/Hermes need writable config/state/cache/session dirs. They are shared rw agent_state_binds by default, outside BranchFS merge policy. Use cred_mounts only for narrow special-case read-only overlays; API-key deployments can use cred_mask + cred_env for individual secret files.
_agent_plugins_comment: Mount-only CCC plugin assets for tools that load persistent config. By default this is Codex only: setup enables/trusts the plugin in Codex config, while ccc-agent run only binds the read-only plugin cache. Claude hooks are written to Claude settings and Hermes gets no default per-run plugin env. No default entry appends agent CLI argv or sets launch env. agent_hook_mode=plugins (default) | disabled. Per-turn hooks are best-effort: if a plugin fails to load, process-exit review still finalizes the session.
_roots_comment: ONE BranchFS root over the whole of /storage: base is the real read-through underlay, store is a node-local delta dir OUTSIDE /storage, visible is where the branch is mounted back inside the sandbox. home_subdir (relative to the branch) is bind-mounted to /home/<user>, so the home and /storage/user/<container> share a single branch instead of being overlaid twice.

policy._policy_comment: workspace-auto: changes under the workspace auto-commit; anything else under /storage (datasets, group, other users) is read-through but flagged for review on write. Agent state dirs are outside BranchFS by default via agent_state_binds; cache/history noise plus ccc-agent-created bind/plugin mountpoints are ignored and discarded.
